question: Should denylist policy permanently exist in both requested tools.exec configuration and host-local exec approvals as a stricter-wins union, or should one surface be the canonical owner?
rationale: This adds persisted and user-configurable policy to a privileged execution boundary; existing exec policy uses layered resolution, but the new STOP-list ownership and rolling-upgrade behavior require explicit maintainer acceptance.

options.title: Keep two layers safely
options.body: Retain stricter-wins union semantics, add mixed-version writer protection, and document the coordinated upgrade and ownership contract.

options.title: Use host approvals only
options.body: Remove tools.exec.denylist and keep mutable STOP rules solely in the execution host approvals policy.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Do not add the policy until a simpler ownership and upgrade model is agreed.

recommendation.title: Keep two layers safely
recommendation.body: Retain stricter-wins union semantics, add mixed-version writer protection, and document the coordinated upgrade and ownership contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their current-main history is most directly tied to exec approval policy, node-host authorization, and permissive execution behavior.
